canonical_statement: The emergence of divine order can disturb primordial chaotic entities.

attributions.surface_quote: poem embodies the beliefs... concerning the origin of the universe; it describes the coming forth of the gods from chaos, and tells the story of how the forces of disorder... were overthrown by Ea and Marduk respectively, and how Marduk... proceeded to create the world and man.

canonical_statement: Disorderly forces, personified as primeval water-gods, preceded the structured creation of the world.

attributions.chapter: VI. THE SEVENTH TABLET OF THE CREATION SERIES
attributions.surface_quote: forces of disorder, represented by the primeval water-gods Apsu and Tiamat, were overthrown by Ea and Marduk

attributions.surface_quote: condition of things before Creation when the primeval water-gods, Apsu and Tiamat, personifying chaos, mingled their waters in confusion.

attributions.surface_quote: his existence, like that of Mummu and of Gaga, appears to be tacitly assumed.

attributions.surface_quote: his birth, moreover, forms the climax to which the previous lines lead up

attributions.surface_quote: from the fact that he makes use of the expressions 'by day' and 'by night,' it may be inferred that day and night were vaguely conceived as already in existence.

attributions.surface_quote: It was therefore the substitution of order in place of chaos which... roused Apsu's resentment and led to his rebellion

attributions.surface_quote: Beilos (i.e. Bel) slew Omorka

attributions.surface_quote: this portion of the poem related the story of the creation of man.

canonical_statement: Human

attributions.chapter: VI. THE SEVENTH TABLET OF THE CREATION SERIES

attributions.surface_quote: The 'cunning plan,' which Marduk devised in order to furnish worshippers for the gods, concerned the creation of man

attributions.surface_quote: the death of Tiamat is made a necessary preliminary to the creation of the world.

attributions.surface_quote: Tiamat, the monster of the deep personifying chaos and confusion

attributions.surface_quote: produced order in place of chaos

attributions.surface_quote: the Moon-god was appointed 'to determine the days.'

attributions.surface_quote: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser to rule the night.

attributions.surface_quote: Marduk, the Creator, of his own blood in the creation of man

attributions.surface_quote: The Quickener of the Dead.

canonical_statement: A divine being can destroy evil entities.

attributions.surface_quote: Who through his Pure Incantation hath destroyed all the evil ones!

canonical_statement: A divine being possesses knowledge of the inner states of other divine beings.

attributions.surface_quote: Shag-zu, 'who knoweth the heart of the gods,' 'who seeth through the innermost part!'

canonical_statement: A divine being can subdue rebellious entities.

attributions.surface_quote: Subduer of the disobedient.

canonical_statement: A divine being can put an end to negative emotional states.

attributions.surface_quote: Who put an end to anger.

canonical_statement: A divine being can create the physical world.

attributions.surface_quote: He named the four quarters (of the world), mankind [he created].

canonical_statement: A singular entity is responsible for the creation of the Earth.

attributions.surface_quote: The Creator of [the earth ...]

canonical_statement: A singular entity is the source of counsel and provision.

attributions.surface_quote: The Giver of counsel and of whatsoever

canonical_statement: A singular entity created the heavens.

attributions.surface_quote: Mulil, the heavens [...], 'Who for ... [...]!'

canonical_statement: A singular entity has the power to nullify other gods.

attributions.surface_quote: Who brought the gods to naught

canonical_statement: A singular entity holds supreme might over all other lords and gods.

attributions.surface_quote: supreme is his might! ... among the gods is gloriously supreme!

canonical_statement: A singular entity created the gods who are considered its fathers.

attributions.surface_quote: Adu-nuna, 'the Counsellor of Ea,' who created the gods his fathers

canonical_statement: No other deity can comprehend or reach the majesty of this supreme entity.

attributions.surface_quote: No god can ever attain!

canonical_statement: A singular entity has dominion over the beginning and the future.

attributions.surface_quote: May he hold the Beginning and the Future

canonical_statement: A singular entity established the paths for celestial bodies.

attributions.surface_quote: For the stars of heaven he upheld the paths

canonical_statement: A singular entity has authority over all other gods.

attributions.surface_quote: He shepherded all the gods like sheep!

canonical_statement: A singular entity created the celestial realm and the terrestrial realm.

attributions.surface_quote: Since he created the realm (of heaven) and fashioned the firm earth

canonical_statement: A singular entity controls all divine decrees and commands.

attributions.surface_quote: The binding of all my decrees shall he control, All my commands shall he make known!

canonical_statement: The divine word of Marduk is immutable and cannot be overturned by any other deity.

attributions.surface_quote: His word standeth fast, his command is unaltered; The utterance of his mouth hath no god ever annulled.

canonical_statement: No other deity can withstand the wrath of Marduk.

attributions.surface_quote: When he is wroth, no god can withstand his indignation.

canonical_statement: Marduk possesses immense compassion.

attributions.surface_quote: Wide is his heart, broad is his compassion;

canonical_statement: Marduk has complete control over the entirety of existence, from its inception to its future.

attributions.surface_quote: The expression reshu-arkat, literally 'the beginning--the future,' may be taken as implying Marduk's complete control over the world, both at its creation and during its subsequent existence.

canonical_statement: Reality is structured with distinct upper and lower cosmic waters.

attributions.surface_quote: Ti-amat e-li-ti and Ti-amat shap-li-ti, 'The Ocean (Tiamat) which is above' and 'The Ocean (Tiamat) which is beneath'

canonical_statement: A primordial dragon entity, Tiamat, exists within the cosmic order.

attributions.surface_quote: Who was the dragon [...]? Tiamat [*2] was the dragon [...]!

canonical_statement: Divine beings can be appointed to confront and eliminate cosmic threats.

attributions.surface_quote: Who will go and [slay] the dragon... Go, Tishhu, [slay] the dragon

canonical_statement: The act of slaying a cosmic entity can lead to kingship or authority.

attributions.surface_quote: And become king [over ...]

canonical_statement: Divine power can be invoked or utilized to overcome cosmic adversaries.

attributions.surface_quote: Stir up cloud, and storm [and tempest]! The seal of thy life [shalt thou set] before thy face, Thou shalt grasp it, and thou shalt [slay] the dragon.

canonical_statement: The world, including heavens, earth, and living creatures, was created by a council of gods.

attributions.surface_quote: When the gods in their assembly had made [the world], And had created the heavens, and had formed [the earth], And had brought living creatures into being

canonical_statement: Specific categories of life, such as cattle, beasts of the field, and city creatures, were fashioned by divine beings.

attributions.surface_quote: And [had fashioned] the cattle of the field, and the beasts of the field, and the creatures [of the city]

canonical_statement: A distinction or division exists between different types of created beings, specifically beasts of the field and creatures of the city.

attributions.surface_quote: And between the beasts] of the field and the creatures of the city had divided

canonical_statement: Divine beings are responsible for the creation of all creatures.

attributions.surface_quote: Nin-igi-azag [fashion] two small creatures... Among all the beasts he made [their form] glorious

canonical_statement: The cosmos, including celestial bodies and time, is created and ordered by divine beings.

attributions.surface_quote: When the gods Ana, Enlil, and Enki... Ordained the renewal of the Moon-god, the reappearance of the moon, and the creation of the month

canonical_statement: Divine beings establish the boundaries and structure of the heavens and the earth.

attributions.surface_quote: Anu, Bel and Ea... Fixed the bounds of heaven and earth

canonical_statement: The creation of celestial phenomena like the Sun-god is a deliberate act of divine beings.

attributions.surface_quote: mankind beheld the Sun-god in the gate of his going forth, In the midst of heaven and earth they duly created (him)

canonical_statement: A primordial River is the source of all creation and predates the deluge.

attributions.surface_quote: O, thou River, who didst create all things... The deluge they sent not before thou wert!

canonical_statement: Divine beings, such as Ea and Marduk, are associated with the River of Creation and its attributes.

attributions.surface_quote: Within thee Ea... created his dwelling... Have Ea and Marduk presented unto thee!

canonical_statement: The River of Creation possesses attributes of judgment, might, supremacy, and righteousness.

attributions.surface_quote: Thou judgest the cause of mankind! O, River, thou art mighty! O River, thou art supreme! O River, thou art righteous!

canonical_statement: Before creation, there was no structured reality, only an undifferentiated sea.

attributions.surface_quote: No reed had sprung up, no tree had been created... All lands were sea.

canonical_statement: Creation began with a movement within the primordial sea, leading to the formation of specific places and structures.

attributions.surface_quote: At that time there was a movement in the sea; Then was Eridu made, and E-sagil was built.

canonical_statement: Marduk is a creator deity who formed land from water and dust.

attributions.surface_quote: Marduk laid a reed upon the face of the waters, He formed dust and poured it out beside the reed.

canonical_statement: Marduk created the Anunnaki gods simultaneously.

attributions.surface_quote: The gods, the Anunnaki, he created at one time;

canonical_statement: A divine being is responsible for the creation of humanity.

attributions.surface_quote: He formed mankind. The goddess Aruru together with him created the seed of mankind.

canonical_statement: A divine being is responsible for the creation of flora and fauna.

attributions.surface_quote: The beasts of the field and living creatures in the field he formed. The grass... he created.

canonical_statement: A divine being is responsible for the creation and placement of geographical features.

attributions.surface_quote: He created the Tigris and the Euphrates, and he set them in their place.

canonical_statement: A divine being is responsible for the creation of cities and structures.

attributions.surface_quote: Bricks he laid, buildings he set up; Houses he made, cities he built.

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess wisdom and counsel.

attributions.surface_quote: Thy exalted minister is Papsukal, the wise counsellor of the gods.

canonical_statement: Divine beings can perform purification rituals.

attributions.surface_quote: May Nin-aha-kudu, the daughter of Ea, Purify thee with the pure censer.

canonical_statement: Divine incantations can influence earthly abundance and destiny.

attributions.surface_quote: By the incantation of Marduk... May the abundance of the land enter into thee, And may thy decree be accomplished.
